answer: Separate batch and speed paths (Lambda) run the same business logic twice, in two codebases. Correctness comes from the batch layer recomputing complete hours and overwriting the stream's results, and the serving layer merges the views at the boundary hour, preferring batch. Reprocessing means rerunning the batch job. Drift between the layers is a standing risk, and the boundary hour can disagree. One job definition run at two cadences has one code path, one test suite and one deploy. Correctness comes from handling late data inside the stream, and reprocessing is a replay of the retained log through the same job. The output is one table with no merge. This needs log retention long enough for the rebuild, and late-data handling good enough that a batch overwrite is not needed.
